title: What does an expression like seven p minus three q tell us?
description: A quiz gives p marks for a correct answer and takes q marks for a wrong one. The meaning of seven p minus three q is read out, and the marks of three rounds are found when p is four and q is one. Keeko's doubt is that seven p minus three q is four p.
teaching_notes: One idea: in seven p minus three q, seven correct answers add seven p and three wrong answers take away three q. Watch for students who subtract the numbers and keep only one letter.

source: In the quiz, p = 4 is the score for a correct answer and q =
video_script.why: A learner sees what each part of a quiz expression means before putting numbers in.
video_script.substitution: the book's quiz with p as four marks for a correct answer and q as one mark of penalty for a wrong answer
video_script.anchor: the three quiz rounds of the book, with marks seven p minus three q, eight p minus four q and six p minus two q
video_script.wrong_answer: seven p minus three q is four p
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko subtracts the numbers seven and three and keeps only the letter p. Marks for correct answers and penalty for wrong ones are different things, so the idea is broken with p as four and q as one.
video_script.payoff_line: The rounds give twenty five, twenty eight and twenty two marks, and with no penalty q is zero

final_answer.value: Round marks 25, 28 and 22; with no penalty q = 0
final_answer.spoken: the round marks are twenty five, twenty eight and twenty two, and with no penalty q is zero

names.{{NAME_1}}: plays a quiz in three rounds and gets marks like seven p minus three q

maths_rules: 7p - 3q means 7 correct answers worth p each, minus 3 wrong answers costing q each
Keeko test with p = 4, q = 1: 7p - 3q = 25 but 4p = 16, which is not 25
video_script.design: The three quiz rounds stay on the board; the meaning of the first expression is read out, then the numbers are put in round by round.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a quiz with p for a correct answer, q for a wrong answer, and {{NAME_1}}'s first round 7p − 3q

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the quiz board is drawn
marks.letters: the letters p and q are written beside the right and wrong answers
marks.ask: a question mark appears beside the expression

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a quiz question from your book.
<bookmark mark='letters'/>A correct answer earns p marks, and a wrong answer costs q marks as penalty.
<bookmark mark='round'/>{{NAME_1}} plays three rounds, and the first round gives seven p minus three q.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What does that expression tell us?

beats.on_screen: the quiz board stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits beside the quiz board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 7 correct answers marked p each: 7 × p = 7p; 3 wrong answers marked q each: 3 × q = 3q

marks.right: seven ticks appear, each marked p
marks.wrong: three crosses appear, each marked q

narration: <bookmark mark='right'/>Seven correct answers earn seven times p, which is seven p.
<bookmark mark='wrong'/>Three wrong answers cost three times q, which is three q.
<bookmark mark='write'/>The letters p and q stand for numbers, and we fix them later.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, p is four and q is one. The marks of the three rounds are written on the board.

beats.on_screen: To find: what 7p − 3q means, the marks of the three rounds, and q with no penalty

marks.find: the words what 7p − 3q means are written
marks.then: the words three rounds and no penalty are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to say what seven p minus three q means.
<bookmark mark='then'/>Then we find the marks of the three rounds, and the value of q with no penalty.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, meaning of 7p − 3q: 7 correct answers worth p each, minus 3 wrong answers costing q each

marks.right: 7p is circled and labelled correct answers
marks.wrong: 3q is circled and labelled wrong answers
marks.minus: the minus sign between them is lit

narration: <bookmark mark='right'/>Step one, seven p is the marks from seven correct answers.
<bookmark mark='wrong'/>Three q is the penalty from three wrong answers.
<bookmark mark='minus'/>The minus sign takes the penalty away from the marks.
<bookmark mark='put'/>Step two, put p as four and q as one in round one.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Seven times four is twenty eight, and three times one is three.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>Twenty eight minus three is twenty five.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Step three, round two is eight times four minus four times one. That is thirty two minus four, or twenty eight.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Round three is six times four minus two times one. That is twenty four minus two, or twenty two.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, with no penalty q = 0, so 7p − 3q becomes 7p
narration: <bookmark mark='none'/>Step four, with no penalty, nothing is taken away, so q is zero.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Then three q is zero and only seven p is left.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 25, 28 and 22 marks; with no penalty q = 0
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The rounds give twenty five, twenty eight and twenty two marks, and with no penalty q is zero.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the quiz board
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 7p − 3q = 4p, struck out; the test p = 4, q = 1 gives 25 and 16

marks.gap: 25 and 16 appear side by side and do not match
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and 7p − 3q stays

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks seven p minus three q is four p. Seven minus three is four.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Try p as four and q as one.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>Round one gave twenty five, but four p is only sixteen.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Marks for correct answers and penalty for wrong ones are different things, so they stay apart.
